messages:
Sophia: heads up — onboarding converted Llama-2.1-rlhf to the int4 testbed. quick eval shows QA accuracy drop vs fp16 (~78.4% -> 71.2%) on our NQ suite. suspect rotary+dtype interplay.

Kai: can you paste the eval command + small diff?

Sophia: running `./eval.sh --model llama2-2.1-conv --quant int4 --scheme headwise --batch 8`
Results (short):
- fp16: acc 78.4
- int4 (headwise, rotary_scale=1.0): acc 71.2
Logs show early EOS bias and softmax mass shifting on rare tokens.

Omar: did the conversion include a tokenizer swap? qwen tokenizer on a llama checkpoint will sometimes mask sentinel ids if token_map is off by 1. we saw that before.

Sophia: converter v0.9 used. `token_map.json` reported no shifts. kv-cache traces look off for long contexts (repeated proper names compressing). small log snippet:
```
position  45 logits top5: [('the', 0.42), ('</s>', 0.26), ('John', 0.04), ('John', 0.03), ('John', 0.02)]
rotary_phase_drift: 0.0078 per-head avg on head 3
```

Kai: try toggling `rotary_scale` (0.98/1.02) and also `rope_interp='rescale' vs 'legacy'` — might surface a headwise aliasing.

Eva: also check head-ordering on GEMMA conversions — we had `transpose` vs `preserve` defaults causing off-by-one kvcache indexing. add `--preserve-headorder` if possible.

Sophia: running a small grid: rotary_scale [0.96,0.98,1.0,1.02,1.04], rope_interp in {rescale,legacy}, preserve_headorder toggled. hypothesis: packing+rotary quant reduces phase resolution causing token aliasing at sentence boundaries.

ci-bot: nightly eval queued: job #5723 for llama2-2.1-conv int4-grid (ETA 40m) :hourglass: 

Omar: also try a synthetic repro: short prompt with repeated token IDs (like repeating the same name) to isolate kvcache vs vocab aliasing. if repro is consistent we can bisect head groups.

Sophia: made a tiny repro gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/rotary-int4-repro — includes python snippet to force repeated token sequence and compare topk distributions. starting runs now.

Kai: quick thing to try: `--force-rotary-fp32` while keeping weights int4. if gap closes then rotary quantization is culprit.

Sophia: good call — kicked that job. ETA 20m. plan if positive: (1) fallback to rotary fp32 by default for converted llama variants, (2) add unit test in reg-harness to catch top1/top5 distribution shifts, (3) add tokenmap validator in conversion pipeline.

Eva: add top5 KL/regression to the harness — we caught similar with Gemma conversions.

Sophia: quick update: fp32-rotary + int4-weights reduced the acc gap from 7.2% -> 2.1% on the quick NQ subset. still investigating residual.

Omar: that strongly implicates rotary quant. after we stabilize, we should produce a small microreport: per-head rotary error, per-token rare-token lift/drop, and conversion flags used. add it to model-onboard checklist.

Kai: please open PR to pin converter to preserve rotary fp32 for now and add the regression tests. cc @Omar @Eva

Sophia: opened PR #1428 (WIP) with initial eval logs and a reproducible script. CI triggered.

ci-bot: PR #1428 build passed, integration tests scheduled.

Sophia: will follow up with the full grid results and a short writeup. thanks all :pray:
